text: . The Lok Sabha will resume discussion on the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026, today. Minister of State for Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Dr Jitendra Singh, moved the Bill for consideration and passing in the House yesterday.The Bill seeks to amend the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024. It incorporates several significant provisions, including stringent penalties such as imprisonment for up to ten years, fines of up to ten crore rupees and seizure of the properties of convicted offenders.To ensure expeditious disposal of cases, the legislation mandates every State Government and Union Territory Administration to establish Special Fast Track Courts for day-to-day trials. It further provides that investigations into offences must be completed within two months from the date the information is recorded at the police station. Trials must be concluded within three months from the filing of the chargesheet.Moving the Bill, Dr Jitendra Singh said the new legislation reaffirms the government’s deep commitment to safeguarding the welfare of the students and youth of the country. He said it also reiterates Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s resolve not to allow anyone to compromise the future of the youth. Listing a series of paper leaks that occurred during the Congress and UPA era, Dr Singh said there was no comprehensive law to tackle such cases. He said the Modi Government brought the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024, to ensure speedy justice.Participating in the discussion, Congress MP Gaurav Gogoi accused the government of not being serious about the education sector.BJP MP Bansuri Swaraj termed the legislation a transformative step and said such legislation is the need of the hour to ensure fair and transparent examinations. She said the examination mafia has become organised and evolved into a cross-state criminal network. Ms Swaraj said the Bill mandates every State and Union Territory to establish Special Fast Track Courts for speedy trials.Samajwadi Party MP Akhilesh Yadav expressed concern over paper leaks in various examinations. Mr Yadav said the NEET UG paper was leaked this year despite the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act being made in 2024.Abhishek Banerjee of AITC, Lavu Sri Krishna Devarayalu of TDP and Dr Shrikant Shinde of Shiv Sena supported the Bill. The TDP MP also called for decentralised question paper-setting committees.Dayanidhi Maran of DMK asserted that the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET) is the core issue, which is not uniform and is against students.Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra accused the government of failing to protect the interests of students and weakening the education system. She added that the youth had come out to protest to restore their faith in the education system and seek accountability. She also levelled allegations against newly appointed Education Minister Pralhad Joshi, which led to a heated exchange in the Lok Sabha. Union Ministers Pralhad Joshi and Kiren Rijiju asked her to authenticate her remarks or apologise to the House.BJP MP Tejasvi Surya said students want a system that protects their future and not politics. He said a fair examination is the only gateway to opportunity for crores of families.Other members, including NCP (SP) MP Supriya Sule, Samajwadi Party’s Dimple Yadav, BJP’s Anurag Thakur and Shashank Mani, Congress MP KC Venugopal, S Venkatesan of CPI(M), Gurumoorthy Maddila of YSRCP, RJD’s Abhay Kumar Sinha, AIMIM’s Asaduddin Owaisi and Harsimrat Kaur Badal of SAD, also participated in the discussion.The discussion remained inconclusive. Presiding Officer Sandhya Ray adjourned the House to meet at 11 AM today.

. India’s first-ever direct commercial container freight train has reached Nepal, marking a new chapter in rail-based cross-border freight movement. The Railway Ministry said that the train, comprising 40 wagons carrying a consignment of canola, completed its journey under the revised India-Nepal Rail Transit Protocol.  The successful operation enables direct rail movement of containerised cargo from Kolkata Port to Biratnagar without transshipment at the border. The new arrangement is expected to reduce transit time, logistics costs and cargo handling while improving the efficiency, reliability and competitiveness of cross-border trade between the two neighbouring countries.The Ministry said that the direct freight service is also expected to provide a significant boost to the movement of import and export cargo by offering a faster, more economical and environmentally sustainable mode of transportation. It added that by reducing multiple handling points and improving supply chain efficiency, the initiative will benefit exporters, importers, logistics operators and industries engaged in cross-border trade.

. Union Youth Affairs and Sports Minister Dr Mansukh Mandaviya has congratulated Sarvesh Kushare on winning the Silver Medal in the Men’s High Jump at the Glasgow Commonwealth Games.In a social media post, the Minister noted that his phenomenal performance that has made the entire nation proud.

. Most Asian stock markets closed lower today. South Korea’s Kospi index plummeted 10.8 per cent as investors sold tech shares amid heightened fears over artificial intelligence investment. Earlier in the session, the index had fallen by more than 8 per cent, prompting the Korea Exchange (KRX) to activate a circuit breaker and halt trading for 20 minutes. It marked the seventh time this year that the exchange has activated a circuit breaker.Taiwan’s Taiex shed over 4.6 per cent, Japan’s Nikkei 225 fell more than 3.9 per cent, China’s Shanghai Composite dipped almost 1.2 per cent, and Singapore’s Strait Times index settled marginally lower. In contrast, Hong Kong’s Hang Seng Index climbed 0.4 per cent.Major European indices were trading with gains today. London’s FTSE 100 added half a per cent, while Germany’s DAX as well as France’s CAC 40 increased by 0.2 per cent, when reports last came in.

. Punjab has been connected with 27 global destinations across North America, UK, Europe and Australia with the launch of Air India’s ‘Easy Connect’ hub-and-spoke model at Sri Guru Ram Dass Ji International Airport, Amritsar, today.Union Minister of Civil Aviation, Kinjarapu Ram Mohan Naidu who addressed the gathering virtually, said that statistics show that approximately 150,000 passengers travel from Amritsar to Delhi every year to catch international flights. Similarly, about 150,000 passengers arrive in Delhi from abroad and then travel to Amritsar. He said the city will become the international gateway for North India. Major catchment areas including Punjab, Jammu & Kashmir, and Himachal Pradesh will connect through Amritsar. He said of the approximately 30 million Indians living abroad, nearly 10 million are Punjabi and as air connectivity increases, Amritsar’s economy will directly benefit.Civil Aviation Secretary Samir Kumar Sinha who was part of the launch at Amritsar along with AAI Chairman Vipin Kumar said that the hub is an important scheme of the government for the aviation sector as it would ease the travelling of international passengers from their state to the international destinations.With the launch, two daily ‘Easy Connect’ flights have been operationalised from Amritsar. Passengers travelling on such flights of Air India are required to complete certain pre-departure and transit processes to ensure a seamless journey, including mandatory DigiYatra enrolment for Indian nationals. Indian passport holders connecting internationally on Easy Connect flights are required to enrol in DigiYatra. Bookings for Air India’s Easy Connect flights are available across all channels, including Air India’s website, mobile app, contact centre, and travel agents.

. The Delhi Government has approved the Delhi Lakshmi Yojana, aimed at the economic empowerment and social security of women. The decision was taken at a Cabinet meeting chaired by Chief Minister Rekha Gupta at the Delhi Secretariat yesterday. Under the scheme, eligible women will receive financial assistance of 2,500 rupees every month. A provision of 5,110 crore rupees has been made for the scheme in the 2026-27 Budget.Speaking to the media in New Delhi, Chief Minister Rekha Gupta said the registration portal for the scheme will open on 1st August. She said women between 21 and 60 years of age, with an annual family income of up to 2.5 lakh rupees, will be eligible to avail of the benefits.The Chief Minister said the scheme is aimed not only at providing financial assistance but also at promoting education, healthcare, skill development, savings and greater social participation among women. She expressed confidence that the initiative would benefit more than 17 lakh women and help make them self-reliant and empowered.

. In Jharkhand, security forces have achieved a major breakthrough in anti-Naxal operations. Top Maoist leader and Politburo member Misir Besra, carrying a bounty of one crore rupees, has been arrested from the Dhanbad-Giridih border.Regional Committee Member Mehnat alias Mochhu, carrying a reward of 15 lakh rupees, Maoist cadre Gaurav and two villagers were also apprehended during the joint operation.The operation was carried out by the CoBRA, CRPF and Jharkhand Police based on specific intelligence inputs.

. French authorities today ordered around 4,000 people to evacuate tourist areas on the Atlantic coast as rising temperatures threatened to reignite a massive wildfire west of Bordeaux. The Gironde fire, which has burned about 420 square kilometres, was stabilized but still not contained. The blaze, raging since last week, has been wildly unpredictable, transforming at times into a self-feeding firestorm as it burned through an area four times the size of Paris. In France, It forced 2 lakh 20 thousand people to evacuate homes and vacation accommodation and injured 93 firefighters. Fire crews continued building firebreaks to stop the blaze from spreading.Wildfires have forced about one lakh 10 thousand evacuations in Spain also. Spain, facing its fourth heat wave of the summer, continued battling several major blazes, including its largest wildfire on record. Authorities have evacuated about 79,000 people and ordered another 30,000 to remain in their homes during this unprecedented crisis that prompted the government to declare a national emergency for wildfires for the first time.

. Power Minister Manohar Lal has said that there is adequate availability of power in the country. In a written reply in the Lok Sabha today, Mr Lal said that the present installed generation capacity of the country is over 548 GW as on June, 2026. The country has addressed the critical issue of power deficiency by adding 324.7 GW of generation capacity since April, 2014 transforming the country from power deficit to power sufficient.He said that as on the 30th of last month, the addition of 2,18,267 circuit kilometre (ckm) of Transmission lines, 9.47,405 MegaVolt-Ampere (MVA) of Transformation capacity and 84,390  MW of Inter-Regional capacity has been done since 2014. Thus, total inter-regional transmission capacity has become 1,20,304 MW, enabling reliable transfer of power across regions.

. The Reserve Bank of India has said that the operations of Paytm Payments Bank Limited will be wound up and has appointed former Chief General Manager of SBI, Girikumar Nair, as the Official Liquidator. The central bank said the decision follows the orders of the Delhi High Court allowing the winding-up of the bank as per the provisions of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, and the Companies Act, 2013.The RBI had announced the cancellation of the banking licence of Paytm Payments Bank, citing serious regulatory violations and concerns over the manner in which the bank’s affairs were conducted. The banking regulator had earlier clarified that despite the winding-up process, Paytm Payments Bank had sufficient liquidity to repay its entire deposit liabilities.

. Saudi Arabia today said, it has shot down drones fired by Iran-backed militias in Iraq. The statement posted on social media today by the Saudi Defence Ministry came as the US and Iran had paused their attacks over the weekend after weeks of escalation. The statement said, the drones targeted petroleum facilities in eastern Saudi Arabia and the capital, Riyadh.

. Rebel TMC MP Saayoni Ghosh attended the NDA Parliamentary Party’s ‘Mangal Milan’ meeting for the first time. Speaking to Reporters at Parliament premises, she described the experience as enriching and said that Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s address focused on the Free Trade Agreement (FTA), the Blue Economy and the government’s vision for country’s future.

. The PoJK is currently engulfed with a wave of protests against the Pakistani authorities since months. Pakistan’s military and authority has been accused of inciting violence by disrupting peaceful protests, carrying out mass arrests and imposing a severe communication blackout by shutting down the internet to cut the region from rest of the world. The unrest in PoJK has spread to Mirpur after the deadly violence in Rawalakot, with several social media accounts alleging that Pakistani security forces opened fire on civilians during fresh protests.Meanwhile, Amnesty International has called for an independent and transparent investigation into reports of the use of lethal force against protesters in PoJK by Pakistani forces while urging Pakistani authorities to restore communication services and allow media and independent observers access to the region.In a statement, Amnesty International’s Acting Regional Director for South Asia, Isabelle Lassee, reacted to the security forces using lethal force against protesters in Rawalakot during the first day of the regional election. She said the ongoing internet and mobile services blackout was preventing independent verification of the situation on the ground. Amnesty also raised concerns over the ban imposed on the Jammu and Kashmir Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC), stating that tensions surrounding the election had been heightened by the move.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi chaired the second high-level meeting with Secretaries to the Government at his residence earlier today. During the meeting, the Prime Minister reviewed the future action agenda of Ministries and Departments dealing with Finance and Economy, Commerce and Industry, and Technology sectors. The meeting focused on accelerating progress towards the goals of Viksit Bharat.During the meeting, Mr Modi called for a strong focus on team building across Ministries and Departments, urging officers to work with a shared sense of purpose. He emphasised the need to break both horizontal and vertical silos within the Government so that departments function in close coordination and deliver integrated outcomes.Highlighting the importance of citizen-centric governance, the Prime Minister said that the people of India must remain at the centre of governance. He reminded that every decision and policy should be guided by the interests and aspirations of the common citizen. Mr Modi stressed that while India is making significant investments in infrastructure, equal priority must be given to developing indigenous technologies. The Prime Minister underscored the importance of technological self-reliance and building domestic capabilities in critical sectors.Mr Modi also underlined that energy security is closely linked with national security, economic stability and citizens’ welfare. He said that the country must achieve self-reliance in the energy sector through innovation, diversification and accelerated capacity creation. The Prime Minister also stressed the need to reform processes, improve work culture and strengthen institutional efficiency.Mr Modi emphasized that growing use of technology must be accompanied by a strong focus on cybersecurity to safeguard digital systems and infrastructure. He also stressed the need for constant vigilance against emerging cyber threats. The Prime Minister also called for encouraging greater participation of young innovators and entrepreneurs in the cybersecurity ecosystem and emphasised that it should evolve into a nationwide movement.Prime Minister Modi further emphasised the importance of proactive communication on strategic sectors where the country is undertaking major initiatives, to counter misinformation and unfounded fears surrounding such efforts. He said that new academic courses should be planned in partnership with industry to equip the workforce with skills required by emerging and future industries. He also observed that a government must always remain youthful, dynamic and forward-looking, continuously adapting to new challenges and opportunities with agility and innovation.The meeting featured detailed discussions by Secretaries on the progress, priorities and implementation issues across their respective domains. The meeting was attended by the Cabinet Secretary, Secretaries of key Ministries and Departments, and senior officials from the Prime Minister’s Office.

. Indian astronomers, along with their international collaborators, have reported the rare discovery of a Blue Straggler Star (BSS) caught in the act of formation. This has provided direct evidence of how such stars are created.Blue Straggler Stars (BSS) are a peculiar class of stars found in star clusters that appear hotter, brighter, and more massive than their peers. The Ministry of Science and Technology informed that astronomers have sought to understand their origin and evolution for a long time.The Ministry said that the most widely accepted explanation is that these stars gain mass from a companion or through stellar mergers, effectively rejuvenating themselves. Direct observational evidence of such formation processes has remained extremely rare.

. The 16th Hockey India Junior Men National Championship 2026 began this morning in Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu. The tournament features country’s finest junior men’s hockey teams who compete over 12 days till 8th of August to decide the national champions. Action on the opening day began with Assam taking on Mizoram in a Division ‘C’ Pool A match.A total of 30 teams are participating across Division ‘A’, ‘B’, and ‘C’, with promotion and relegation adding further significance to every fixture. While Division ‘A’ teams will compete for the championship title, teams in Divisions ‘B’ and ‘C’ will battle for promotion to the next division.Speaking ahead of the championship, Hockey India President Dr. Dilip Tirkey said, the tournament continues to play a crucial role in strengthening India’s hockey ecosystem by providing young players with a highly competitive platform to showcase their abilities.Hockey India Secretary General Bhola Nath Singh added that the Junior Men National Championship is an important step in the development pathway for aspiring hockey players across the country.The tournament will follow a league format during the pool stage, with teams earning three points for a win, one point for a draw, and no points for a loss. In Division ‘A’ classification matches where a winner is required, tied contests will be decided through a shoot-out in accordance with the FIH Tournament Regulations.

. Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw has said that the government has released the TV Ratings Policy 2026, which sets out comprehensive guidelines for regulating television ratings in India. In a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today, Mr Vaishnaw said, the policy defines clear standards for the registration, operation, audit, and oversight of agencies providing TV rating services, to ensure transparency, independence and accountability in audience measurement. He said, the TV Rating Policy 2026 replaced the existing Guidelines for TV Rating Agencies in India dated 16th January 2014.The Minister informed that the major reforms were introduced under the Policy. It includes reduction of net worth criteria from 20 crore rupees to five crore rupees, technology-neutral audience measurement across multiple platforms including connected TVs and TV channels available on OTT platforms, and increased sample size by expansion of metered homes from 50 thousand to 80 thousand. There will be periodic establishment surveys every three years, exclusion of landing page in computation of viewership data, annual independent audits and an A-graded penalty framework for non-compliance. Mr Vaishnaw said, the prescribed safeguards include cross-holding restrictions, requirement of at least 33 per cent independent directors on the board of the agency, prohibition of consultancy or advisory activities that may create conflicts of interest, security clearance requirements, audit and transparency obligations to ensure the functional and operational independence of rating agencies. He said, under this Policy, any entity in the business of television ratings in India has to comply with certain additional requirements and to register under the new Policy. Mr Vaishnaw said, as on date, no entity is registered under the new Policy. He said, the Television Ratings Policy, 2026 places no restriction on the number of agencies that may be registered to provide TV rating services.

. At the ongoing Commonwealth Games 2026 in Glasgow, Gulveer Singh scripted history by becoming the first Indian athlete to win a medal in the men’s 10,000-metre race after claiming a silver medal. The reigning Asian champion clocked 27:49.78 at the Scotstoun Stadium to finish behind Australia’s Ky Robinson.Harjinder Kaur also added a silver to India’s medal tally in the women’s 69-kilogramme weightlifting event. The 29-year-old Indian weightlifter finished with a combined lift of 227 kilograms to secure India’s seventh medal from eight weightlifting events in Glasgow. This was Harjinder Kaur’s second successive Commonwealth Games medal, after she won bronze at Birmingham in 2022. With this, India’s total medal count at the Glasgow Games rose to 12, including two gold, seven silver and three bronze medals.Meanwhile, four Indian boxers have secured guaranteed bronze medals and will aim to convert them into silver or gold when they compete in the semifinals.Lovlina Borgohain secured India’s first guaranteed medal in the women’s 75-kilogramme event, while Preeti Pawar progressed to the women’s 54-kilogramme semifinals. Priya Ghanghas assured herself of at least a bronze medal by defeating Scotland’s Niamh Mitchell 4-1 in her women’s 60-kilogramme quarterfinal match. Jadumani Singh Mandengbam also stormed into the men’s 55-kilogramme semifinals, extending India’s guaranteed boxing medal tally.

. External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar extended greetings to the Government and people of Peru on their Independence Day today. In a social media post, Dr Jaishankar said that India looks forward to strengthening relations with Peru.

. Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) have turned net buyers of Indian equities, purchasing shares worth 14 thousand 946 crore rupees so far in July. According to the latest depository data, FPIs infused 3,049 crore rupees into the domestic stock market last week.Meanwhile, India’s debt market continued to attract strong foreign inflows. So far in July, Foreign Portfolio Investors have invested 9,521 crore rupees in debt securities through the Fully Accessible Route (FAR) and 27,391 crore rupees through the general rout

. The Ministry of Home Affairs has notified the Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB) Combatised General Duty Group ‘C’ Posts Recruitment Rules, 2026, under which fifty per cent of vacancies shall be reserved for ex-Agniveers for recruitment to the post of Constable (General Duty) in every recruitment year.The notification supersedes the recruitment rules issued in 2011 for Assistant Sub-Inspector (General Duty), Head Constable (General Duty) and Constable (General Duty) posts. The new rules came into effect from the date of their publication in the Official Gazette on 27th of this month.According to the notification, recruitment for Constable (General Duty) will be carried out through direct recruitment, deputation, re-employment and remuneration. Ex-Agniveers will also be exempted from the written examination, Physical Standard Test and Physical Efficiency Test.Recruitment for the vacancies reserved for ex-Agniveers will proceed in two phases. The first phase involves the nodal force conducting recruitment for the 50 per cent vacancies earmarked for ex-Agniveers. The second phase will be an open competitive examination covering the remaining 50 per cent of vacancies, along with any unfilled positions from the first phase.The notification said candidates from the first Ex-Agniveer batch will receive up to five years’ relaxation in the upper age limit, while subsequent batches will be granted up to three years’ relaxation.

. In Libya, protesters stormed into a key energy complex near Tripoli amid anti-government demonstrations over prolonged power outages, raising fears of a nationwide blackout. The protesters entered the Mellitah Oil & Gas complex yesterday and closed the gas lines used to operate power plants to generate electricity. The Power company operating the complex warned that the disruption could trigger widespread blackouts and collapse the electricity grid.Demonstrations have spread across western Libya, including Zawiya, Tripoli, and Misrata, over hour long outages. Protesters are demanding improved electricity services and the resignation of Prime Minister Abdul Hamid Dbeibah’s Government of National Unity. Mr. Dbeibah leads the internationally recognised government in Tripoli, while Osama Hammad heads the administration in the east, where the powerful military commander Khalifa Hifter continues to hold sway.Libya has remained divided since the 2011 NATO-backed uprising that toppled and killed longtime dictator Muammar Gaddafi.

. Union Communications Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia today reviewed the progress of the Bharat 6G Alliance (B6GA) in New Delhi and reiterated the government’s commitment to making India a global leader in 6G technologies. The review focused on the progress made by the Bharat 6G Alliance towards achieving Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision of making India a front-line contributor in the design, development and deployment of 6G technology by 2030. The Alliance is working through seven specialised groups covering areas such as spectrum, technology, applications, sustainability, manufacturing, outreach and 6G use cases.On the occasion, Mr Scindia stressed the need to benchmark India’s 6G progress against global developments and strengthen collaboration among the Alliance’s working groups. He emphasised that India’s 6G journey must be driven by indigenous research, global standards participation, domestic manufacturing and strong partnerships among government, industry, academia, startups and research institutions.

. India’s industrial output as measured by the Index of Industrial Production (IIP) grew at a 23-month high of 7.3 percent in June this year. According to government data released today, all four broad sectors posted positive growth in June.Manufacturing, which carries the heaviest weight in the index, grew 7.8 percent, while electricity and gas supply posted a 10.6 percent expansion. Water supply, sewerage and waste management rose by 6.1 per cent. Meanwhile, the mining and quarrying sector grew at a relatively modest pace of one per cent.

. Supreme Court today directed the release of student protesters who are under 18 and have no criminal records. The Court also asked authorities to preserve electronic and digital evidence relating to the recent nationwide protests over the NEET paper leak.The Court also observed that there was a need for a fair and independent investigation into the allegations of injuries to the students and police officials during the student protests last week.Hearing a batch of petitions alleging excessive use of police force during the demonstrations, the apex court issued a slew of interim directions.The bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant, Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, directed all states where protests were held to preserve CCTV footage, drone recordings, body-camera footage, wireless communication records, PCR logs and other digital evidence pertaining to the protests.It also ordered that any digital data collected on protesters be preserved but not brought into the public domain.The bench restrained authorities from taking any coercive action against protesting students, saying that the protection would not extend to persons with criminal antecedents.The bench permitted the Delhi government to continue investigations into FIRs registered but said no coercive action be taken against eligible protesting students during the pendency of the proceedings.The bench also sought responses from the chief secretaries of Delhi, Maharashtra, Bihar, Kerala, Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh to the allegations raised in the petitions.The Court said, the allegations prima facie warrant consideration of a fair and independent probe, which must also address the concerns of families of over 200 injured police personnel.Solicitor General Tushar Mehta said students will not indulge in violence against police personnel, but some miscreants are involved in the incidents.

. World Nature Conservation Day is being observed today globally. This day raises awareness about protecting nature and conserving natural resources to save the earth from the dangers of adverse impacts of climate change.In 1997, the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) declared July 28th as World Nature Conservation Day. The purpose was to emphasize the significance of nature conservation and sustainable practices for the well-being of the planet.

. In Shooting, India’s Sonam Uttam Maskar and Himanshu Dhillon secured the bronze medal in the 10m Air Rifle Mixed Team event at the ongoing ISSF World Cup Rifle/Pistol/Shotgun in Hangzhou, China today.The Indian duo delivered a consistent performance, finishing with a combined score of 441.2 points, with both shooters contributing 220.6 points each to seal the bronze medal. China’s first and second teams claimed the gold and silver medals.With this podium finish, India’s medal tally at the ISSF World Cup in Hangzhou has risen to four medals, including one gold, one silver, and two bronze.

. Union Home Minister Amit Shah has congratulated para-athlete Sharmila Dhankhar on winning India’s first gold medal in para-athletics at the Commonwealth Games. In a social media post, Mr Shah praised her stellar performance in the women’s shot put F57 event and stated that it is a testament to India’s unwavering spirit.Union Youth Affairs and Sports Minister Dr Mansukh Mandaviya also congratulated Sharmila Dhankar. In a social media post, Dr Mandaviya noted that with this victory, Sharmila became country’s first-ever Commonwealth Games Gold medallist in Para Athletics. The Minister added that her indomitable spirit has made the entire nation proud on the global stage.

. President Droupadi Murmu has congratulated Sharmila Dhankar on winning the Gold Medal in the Women’s Shot Put F57 event at the Glasgow Commonwealth Games 2026. In a social media post, the president said that by becoming India’s first-ever Commonwealth Games gold medallist in para-athletics, Sharmila has achieved a landmark feat. President Murmu noted that Sharmila’s achievement will inspire young athletes to excel in their chosen fields. She wished her many more laurels in the years to come.The President also congratulated Sarvesh Anil Kushare for clinching the silver medal in the Men’s High Jump event at the Commonwealth Games 2026. President Murmu noted that with this excellent performance, Kushare has made the nation proud. The president extended best wishes to him for many more inspiring feats.Further, President Murmu congratulated Valluri Ajaya Babu on securing the silver medal in the Men’s 79kg weightlifting event at the Glasgow Commonwealth Games 2026. The president noted that his determination and exceptional performance have brought immense pride to the nation. She wished him many more laurels.President Murmu extended best wishes to Shilpa K Shyla for winning the bronze medal in the Women’s Shot Put F57 event at the Commonwealth Games 2026. Congratulating her in a social media post, the President said that her resolve and perseverance are an inspiration to all.

. The Union Health Ministry today observed World Hepatitis Day 2026, marking 8 years of the National Viral Hepatitis Control Programme (NVHCP). The programme, launched in 2018 under the National Health Mission, aims to eliminate viral hepatitis as a public health threat by 2030, in line with the Sustainable Development Goals.Addressing the event in New Delhi, Union Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare Anupriya Patel reaffirmed the Government’s commitment to achieving a Hepatitis-Mukt Bharat. She said India is among the few countries providing free treatment for Hepatitis C and free management of Hepatitis B. She added that hepatitis screening and treatment services have now been expanded to more than one lakh 85 thousand Ayushman Arogya Mandirs, improving access to care across the country.The Minister said Hepatitis B birth-dose vaccination coverage has crossed 92 per cent. She urged States and Union Territories to ensure 100 per cent screening of pregnant women for Hepatitis B and to step up awareness on Hepatitis B and Hepatitis C for early detection and timely treatment. On the occasion, Union Health Secretary Punya Salila Srivastava said that under the National Viral Hepatitis Control Programme, over 21 crore people have been screened, more than six lakh patients treated and one thousand 153 treatment centres established across the country. She added that over seven crore 64 lakh pregnant women have also been screened under the programme.During the event, the Ministry also released Information, Education and Communication materials on viral hepatitis, highlighting its modes of transmission and the services available under the National Viral Hepatitis Control Programme for wider dissemination across States and Union Territories.

. The Digital India BHASHINI Division under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology today conducted a Multilingual AI Workshop for officials of the Haryana Vidhan Sabha Secretariat to promote language-first legislative governance. The workshop showcased AI-powered language technologies aimed at making legislative processes more inclusive, accessible and citizen-centric.The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology said, the workshop brought together Members of the Legislative Assembly, Assembly Secretariat officials and other stakeholders to explore how multilingual Artificial Intelligence can improve legislative workflows, enhance access to legislative information and enable seamless communication across languages.Speaking on the occasion, Chief Executive Officer of the Digital India BHASHINI Division, Amitabh Nag, said BHASHINI aims to build a language-first Digital Public Infrastructure where every citizen can access digital public services in the language they understand the best. He said multilingual AI can help legislative institutions improve efficiency through real-time transcription, translation, multilingual publication and better citizen engagement.The Ministry said the workshop marks another step towards expanding the adoption of AI-powered language technologies across public institutions and strengthening multilingual, transparent and citizen-centric governance.

. India has termed the so-called legislative assembly elections being conducted in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir (PoJK) an attempt by Pakistan to camouflage its illegal occupation and hide its grave human rights violations in the region. Briefing media in New Delhi this afternoon, External Affairs Ministry Spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal called it a cosmetic electoral exercise and said that Jammu, Kashmir and Ladakh are integral and inalienable parts of India. Mr Jaiswal said that the ongoing mass protests in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir are the direct consequences of Pakistan’s economic exploitation, its denial of the people’s fundamental rights, and its administrative oppression.On SAARC, Mr Jaiswal stated that India favours strong regional cooperation and has been working towards it for several decades. He said everyone in South Asia is aware of which country and what activities are responsible for stymying SAARC. He added that, after all, cooperation does require goodwill.Responding to a question on Pakistan Gen Z, the spokesperson said everyone is aware that Pakistan has been sponsoring cross-border terror against India for decades. He said the people of India, including the Gen Z, have been demanding that the Pakistani state sponsored cross border terrorism must come to an end. He hoped their counterparts are taking due note.On Pakistan and Indus Valley civilisation, Mr Jaiswal said a country which has been promoting cross border terrorism, religious fundamentalism and violence for decades, cannot have any claim to any pluralistic cultural legacy. He said their abysmal track record on the protection of minorities and their cultural rights make such desperate attempts look even more phoney.On the attack on MV AGN Ragnar at the Port of Odesa, the MEA spokesperson said that there were four Indian nationals on board out of which two Indian nationals are safe, while two are still missing. He added that search efforts are ongoing, and the Ministry is in continuous contact with the local authorities there. Mr Jaiswal said that the government has also established contact with the families of the two missing Indian nationals.Replying to a question on border trade with China, the spokesperson said both sides agreed last year to the reopening of border trade through the three designated trading points. These points are Lipulekh Pass, Shipki La Pass and Nathu La pass.On the extradition of Nirav Modi, Mr Jaiswal said that certain judicial proceedings are currently underway in the UK. He informed that once those legal proceedings are concluded, the process of his extradition will move forward. Mr Jaiswal said, the government’s position remains firm that all fugitive offenders should be brought back to India and made to face the judicial process here.

. The All India Football Federation (AIFF) has announced that the Indian Football League (IFL) 2026-27 will begin on 16th of October. The Governing Council of the IFL met at the Football House in New Delhi yesterday. The meeting was attended by representatives from 10 of the 11 IFL clubs.Governing Council and the AIFF deliberated on key decisions for the 2026-27 season including increased gametime for Indian players and a maximum of three foreign players in a team’s starting line-up. The broadcast performance of IFL 2025-26 was also reviewed as the last season recorded 17.56 million live television viewers.AIFF Deputy Secretary General M Satyanarayan said that it was the first meeting ahead of the new season to discuss the roadmap and the proposed budgets.

. In Madhya Pradesh, Gandhi Medical College of Bhopal has developed a new AI-based technology to detect oral cancer at an early stage. The Government of India has granted a patent for the design of this technology. The college’s Department of Dental Surgery has also developed an AI-based mobile app called “Mukh Arogya.”The app will help in the early screening of oral cancer. It can be used by ASHA workers, Community Health Officers and staff at Primary Health Centres. It is expected to benefit people living in villages and remote areas. If early signs of oral cancer are found, patients can be referred to specialist doctors without delay. This will help start treatment on time.It may also reduce serious cases of the disease. Around 150,000 new oral cancer cases are reported in India every year. Early detection remains a major challenge for the healthcare system. Dr. Anuj Bhargav, Head of the Department of Dental Surgery said the main aim is to detect the disease at an early stage. He said early diagnosis makes treatment more effective and less expensive.Dr. Richa Sharma and Dr. Animesh Barodiya also played an important role in developing this project.

Union Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways Sarbananda Sonowal reviewed the safety and welfare measures for Indian seafarers working on merchant vessels in conflict-sensitive regions amid rising geopolitical tensions affecting global shipping routes.The Minister held a comprehensive review meeting yesterday with senior officials of the Ministry of External Affairs, Directorate General of Shipping and Heads of Indian Missions from countries including Oman, Saudi Arabia, Iran, Russia and Ukraine.During the meeting, Mr Sonowal was briefed on the prevailing security situation, maritime developments and the preparedness of Indian missions abroad to assist Indian seafarers during emergencies. He directed all concerned agencies to maintain constant coordination, stressing that the safety of Indian seafarers remains the government’s foremost priority.The Directorate General of Shipping informed that its 24×7 Seafarer Grievance and Assistance Cell is fully operational, providing round-the-clock support through dedicated helplines, information services and grievance redressal mechanisms. The Minister also reviewed measures to enhance seafarer preparedness before deployment.Mr Sonowal further emphasised integrating mental health support into the seafarer welfare framework through counselling services for seafarers and their families. He directed officials to maintain close coordination with Indian Missions abroad, shipping companies, maritime authorities and other stakeholders to ensure a proactive and effective response mechanism for the Indian maritime community.

. India has reiterated its commitment to an open, inclusive, transparent and rules-based multilateral trading system. During the final session of India’s Eighth Trade Policy Review at the World Trade Organization (WTO) in Geneva, Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agarwal said WTO reform should remain development-oriented, preserve policy space for developing countries, strengthen the Organisation’s credibility and deliver on existing mandates. He reaffirmed that reform is a continuous process and highlighted India’s commitment to an open, transparent and predictable trade and investment regime.Mr Agarwal said India’s tariff reforms, customs simplification measures and ambitious Free Trade Agreement strategy have steadily strengthened the country’s integration with the global economy while supporting domestic development objectives. He also highlighted India’s progress in financial inclusion, digital commerce, logistics modernisation and environmental sustainability, while reaffirming the country’s commitment to an inclusive and innovation-driven growth model.During the two review sessions held on 21 and 23 July, 68 WTO members made interventions, reflecting growing global interest in India’s economic transformation. Mr Agarwal thanked the members for their active participation and the keen interest shown in India’s trade policies.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi congratulated Sharmila for winning a gold medal in the Women’s Shot Put F57 event and also for a season-best throw at the Commonwealth Games (CWG) in Glasgow. In a social media post, he called the performance remarkable, which ended a two-decade-long wait for a Para Athletics Gold at the Commonwealth Games. He also congratulated Valluri Ajaya Babu for winning the Silver Medal in the weightlifting Men’s 79 kg category at the Commonwealth Games (CWG) in Glasgow.The Prime Minister said that the weightlifter etched his name in the record books by setting a CWG Record in the Snatch event. Mr Modi further congratulated Sarvesh Anil Kushare for clinching the Silver Medal in the Men’s High Jump event at the Commonwealth Games 2026. The Prime Minister extended his best wishes to all the medalists for many more inspiring feats.

In the Commonwealth Games, Indian swimmer Srihari Nataraj secured his place in the men’s 100m backstroke semifinals after finishing fifth in Heat 4 with a time of 55.58 seconds.India’s para swimmers also delivered strong performances, with RVVBK Budigina and Ali Imam advancing to the men’s 50m freestyle S13 final. Budigina finished third in Heat 1 with a timing of 26.33 seconds, while Ali Imam qualified after placing fifth in Heat 2 with a time of 28.41 seconds.In athletics, Indian sprinter Vishal TK progressed to the men’s 400m semifinals after finishing second in Heat 6 with a time of 46.49 seconds. Rajesh Ramesh, who clocked 47.43 seconds to finish third in Heat 3, narrowly missed out on a semifinal spot.Meanwhile, Sajan Prakash’s men’s 50m butterfly campaign came to an end after he finished eighth in his heat and 28th overall, missing qualification for the semifinals.In weightlifting, India’s Nirupama Devi Seram was also unable to complete her second clean and jerk attempt at 123kg in the women’s 63kg final.India currently sits eighth in the Commonwealth Games medal standings with a tally of 10 medals including two gold, five silver, and three bronze.

. Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri met with Hua Chunying, Vice Minister of Foreign Affairs of China and reviewed the entire gamut of bilateral relations in Beijing. . India has emerged as the world’s second-largest supplier of seafarers, contributing 311,936 maritime professionals to the global shipping industry. According to the BIMCO-ICS Seafarer Workforce Report 2026, India now accounts for 12.16 per cent of the global seafaring workforce, ranking behind only the Philippines and ahead of China, the Russian Federation and Indonesia.The achievement marks one of the most remarkable transformations in the history of India’s maritime sector. In 2015, India contributed only 5.2 per cent of the world’s seafarers and ranked fifth globally, behind China, the Philippines, Indonesia and the Russian Federation. Six years later, in 2021, India’s share had grown modestly to 6 per cent, though it continued to remain in fifth position. The latest BIMCO-ICS report, however, records a decisive breakthrough.

. The National Testing Agency (NTA) has issued advertisements for a set of senior professional appointments at the level of General Manager. It has also opened the engagement of sixteen young professionals through the Pratibha Setu portal of the Union Public Service Commission. NTA in a statement said that these measures represent the first concrete step in the institutional rebuild of the agency that is being implemented in line with the recommendations of the High-Level Committee of Experts chaired by Prof. K. Radhakrishnan.NTA has notified four Positions for General Manager on contract, each for an initial term of three years. The General Manager, Assessment Research and Development and Psychometrics, will head NTA’s academic and measurement-science function. The General Manager, Test Centre Network and Operations, will lead NTA’s nationwide test-centre footprint, spanning over five hundred cities and select international centres, with responsibility for empanelment standards, capacity planning, and centre quality. The General Manager, Information Security, designated as NTA’s Chief Information Security Officer, will head the cyber-security function of the Agency. The General Manager, Vigilance, Investigation and Forensics, will head NTA’s internal vigilance, investigations and digital forensics function.The NTA said that the engagement of Young Professionals is being undertaken for the first time. The Agency added that further recruitment and empanelment actions across the ten functional verticals recommended by the High-Level Committee of Experts will follow in the coming weeks.

She said that over the past four years, she had encouraged the youth to remain rooted in moral values and work towards the progress of the nation and society. She urged women to become self-reliant and move forward on the path of progress with confidence. President Murmu said that When addressing tribal communities, she requested them to preserve their cultural heritage while also becoming part of the mainstream of development.In his address, the Vice President said that President Murmu gave importance to the sentiments of the common people and emphasized on inclusive participation.  The Vice President said that during the past 4 years, President Murmu has enriched the high office with grace, humility, wisdom and commitment to the letter and spirit of the constitution.
